title: A wave of molasses killed 21 people in Boston

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1919, a wave of molasses killed 21 people in Boston.
beats.visual: Brown wave sweeps down a sketched Boston street toward camera

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: On January 15, 1919, in Boston's North End.
beats.visual: Sketch map of the North End; pin on Commercial Street by the harbour

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why was there so much molasses?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A 50-foot tank held over two million gallons. But there was a problem: it leaked, and they painted it brown.
beats.visual: PD photo of the North End molasses tank; drips; brush paints over them in brown

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It burst. A wave, reportedly 25 feet high, raced out at about 35 miles an hour.
beats.visual: Tank splits; speed card '35 mph'; PD photo of the wrecked elevated railway

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The cold. Cooling molasses thickened, trapping people. 21 died, about 150 hurt.
beats.visual: PD wreckage photo; thermometer drops; counters 21 and 150

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Boston then required engineers to sign off on plans. The smell reportedly lingered for decades.
beats.visual: Stamped blueprint 'ENGINEER SIGNED'; faint smell lines over the modern North End

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: 21 lives, lost to molasses. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Wave freezes into syrup; History Sketches corner logo

description: On January 15, 1919, a leaking 50-foot tank of molasses burst in Boston's North End, sending a sticky wave through the streets that killed 21 people. The disaster changed how Boston approved construction. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #boston #strangehistory
